Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Civic life: news, government & the law

social adjective

of society, of living with others

also sociable, social life, social animal, social class

classical

Sen. Clem. 1.3.2: hominem sociāle animal commūnī bonō genitum
Sen. Ben. 5.11.5: beneficium dare sociālis rēs est
Sen. Ben. 7.1.7

sociālis, sociāle

social, made for fellowship

In this sense post-Augustan (Seneca). In Cicero and Livy sociālis means “of the allies”: bellum sociāle, the Social War (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • sociābilis, sociābile — sociable, made for company

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 95.52: amōrem indidit mūtuum et sociābilēs fēcit

    Rare, and not before Augustus (Lewis & Short).

  • convīctus, convīctūs m. — social life, company, living together

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.21: convīctum hūmānum et societātem; Mart. 10.47.8: convīctus facilis

  • societās, societātis f. — society, fellowship, partnership

    noun; its genitive does for “social”: societās generis hūmānī, human society · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.54: prīma societās in ipsō conjugiō est; Cic. Amic. 20: societās generis hūmānī (Lewis & Short)

  • ōrdō, ōrdinis m. — social class, rank

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Dom. 74: equester ōrdō (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. class: social class

Examples

  • inter nōs, quī hominem sociāle animal commūnī bonō genitum vidērī volumus

    among us, who would have man seen as a social animal, born for the common goodSen. Clem. 1.3.2

  • beneficium dare sociālis rēs est, aliquem conciliat, aliquem obligat

    doing a kindness is a social act: it wins someone over, it puts someone in your debtSen. Ben. 5.11.5

  • prūdēns simplicitās, parēs amīcī; convīctus facilis, sine arte mēnsa

    wise simplicity, friends who are your equals; easy company, a table without fussMart. 10.47.7–8

See also people, friend, human.
